name: Boneshatter Juggernaut
summary: League-start melee build. Boneshatter trades a little life for stacks, so the gear is armour and resistances, the axe is a rare with attack speed, and the ascendancy makes the trauma survivable. No unique is required, which is what a strength build needs on day one of a solo league.

pros.text: Very tanky: armour, endurance charges and Juggernaut recovery.
No required unique; a rare two-handed axe is the whole damage slot.
Strong single-target once trauma stacks are running.
Cheap to gear because accuracy is solved by Resolute Technique.
Trauma scaling rewards staying in the fight.
A comfortable lab runner for the first two labyrinths.

cons.text: Trauma hurts you; mistakes and long fights tax your own life.
Melee range means you eat mechanics a ranged build can walk away from.
Attack speed is both damage and survival, so slow weapons feel bad.
Clear speed is slower than a bow or a minion build.
Mana is tight before leech and reduced cost are solved.
Resolute Technique gives up critical strikes entirely.

summary.text: Boneshatter Juggernaut is a two-handed melee build that measures 276.1k at red maps and 524.5k at pinnacle. The rare axe and armour carry the damage and defence, the ascendancy makes the trauma survivable, and no unique is required.

leveling.text: Level with Cleave and the usual strength supports until Boneshatter is available, then switch to the two-handed axe. The first checkpoint measures 420 life and 30 damage; the second measures 477. Keep a life flask and a mana flask equipped until leech takes over.

maps.text: At red maps the build measures 276.1k damage, 26753 effective life and 11079 physical max hit. Cap the elemental resistances, keep the axe current, and let the filter hide the rest.

bossing.text: Pinnacle measures 524.5k damage with 32432 effective life and 12678 physical max hit. Use Enduring Cry before the burst and keep the trauma stacks running while you move out of the biggest slams.
